title: Swapping a regular sequence of length two
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $a,b\in R$. If $a,b$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and $b$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$, then $b,a$ is a regular sequence in $R$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07DW (lemma-regular-sequence-in-polynomial-ring), case $r=2$: "the kernel of $a : R/(b)\to R/(b)$ is isomorphic to the kernel of $b : R/(a)\to R/(a)$ if both $a$ and $b$ are nonzerodivisors"

mathlib_searches.query: if a, b is a regular sequence and b is a nonzerodivisor then b, a is a regular sequence
mathlib_searches.results: RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular, IsRegular.cons', isWeaklyRegular_append_iff', IsLocalRing.isRegular_of_perm (Mathlib.RingTheory.Regular.RegularSequence): permutation only for local Noetherian M, no swap lemma

mathlib_searches.query: swap two elements of a weakly regular sequence: IsWeaklyRegular M [a, b] and b is SMul regular on M implies IsWeaklyRegular M [b, a]
mathlib_searches.results: IsRegular.toIsWeaklyRegular, IsWeaklyRegular.prototype_perm (needs torsion condition K = aK -> K = 0 on all sub-quotients), IsWeaklyRegular.cons, isWeaklyRegular_cons_iff, isRegular_cons_iff

RegularSequence.lean:576 private lemma IsWeaklyRegular.swap {a b} (h1 : IsWeaklyRegular M [a, b]) (h2 : torsionBy R M b = a • torsionBy R M b → torsionBy R M b = ⊥) : IsWeaklyRegular M [b, a] -- private, and its hypothesis h2 is a torsion condition (implied by b being M-regular, since then torsionBy b = ⊥); weakly regular only (no nonvanishing of M/(a,b)M)
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match (private lemma IsWeaklyRegular.swap is a Lean candidate for stage 3: with b regular, h2 holds trivially; IsRegular adds only top_ne_smul, which is symmetric in a,b)
